name: web/chart-3d
title: 3D bar chart
summary: One HTML file with a three.js 3D bar chart of the user's numbers: bars grow from zero on a floor, turn with mouse or finger, each with its label and value, a few reference lines on a back wall.
when: Use when the user wants their own numbers drawn as a 3D bar chart or 3D graph that can be turned and looked at from other sides.

title.about: A short name for the chart, shown in the browser tab and on the page.

data.about: The user's own numbers, one label and one number per bar, in the order given, up to 12 bars: "apples 4, pears 7". One pair per line (separated by \n) works too. Keep numbers as the user wrote them, a sign such as % or $ may stay.

color.about: The colour of the bars, one CSS colour name or hex such as #5ba453. The tallest bar is drawn in a stronger tone of it.

unit.about: Text printed after each value, such as "orders". Write none when the numbers have no unit.

next: Nothing more to do: the page is finished and shows itself in the chat. Do not read it, run it, build it or install anything; tell the user in one or two sentences what the chart shows. Only when the user asks for a change: edit the three plain texts near the top of index.html (the script tags with id data, color and unit) with replace_in_file.
change: Only the three texts near the top of index.html are edited, one call per change: replace_in_file(path="{file}", old="<the data text as it is now>", new="<the new numbers>") changes the bars; the same with the text inside <script type="text/plain" id="color"> changes the colour (a CSS name or hex) and inside id="unit" the text after each value (none for no unit). Do not touch the script below them.

not_text: No numbers were understood. Write one label and number per line, like: Mon 12
The colour was not understood; the default colour is used.
